newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on China latex enquiries.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on China latex enquiries.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher on China inquiries for latex rubber and shortcovering by Europeans for nearby shipment.
Dealers said the rise was also boosted by gains in Tokyo where the stronger expiry price of spot May encouraged local investors to buy.

"There were some enquiries for latex rubber by the Chinese for June shipment. People are offering them (the Chinese) at around 226 cents," a dealer at a trading firm said. But no deals have been transacted as price ideas were not right.
Dealers said some volumes of SMR 10 and SMR 20 rubber for nearby delivery to Europeans ahead of the summer holidays were transacted.
"Prices are likely to hold steady at around current levels or rise further on speculation of more Europeans shortcovering," a trader said.

Traders quoted SMR CV at 328, SMR 5 at 270, SMR L at 307, SMR 10 at 261 and drum latex at 226. June RSS 1 buyer was officially closed at 280.50 cents ($1.12) a kg, up two cents from Monday, and June SMR 20 buyer was up half a cent at 264.50 cents.
